note: Adapted from the species description of Ateuchotermes muricatus in Sands (1972), originally in English; the species has no soldiers, only alates and workers; the comparative passage at the end of the account is merged into the diagnostic characters, and measurement tables, figure numbers, type specimens and distribution records are not translated; figures in the measurement tables that could not be recovered from OCR damage are not recorded.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The species has been compared under A. ctenopher. A. retifaciens and A. tranquillus are distinguished from it by the same set of characters that separates them from A. ctenopher; the remaining species are distinguished in the alate by mandibular proportions. Among the workers, A. sentosus is smaller and the wall of its enteric valve seat bears a sclerotized cup that receives the swollen end of the first enteric valve cushion; in A. rastratus and A. pectinatus the outer margin of the first marginal tooth of the right mandible is longer than that of the second, and in A. spinulatus the apical tooth is longer and slender spines occur on cushions 2–4 of the enteric valve. The development of the enteric valve in the present species appears intermediate between that seen in A. rastratus and A. pectinatus and the slender type of A. spinulatus, varying considerably between specimens from Malawi and South Africa, and the two species might be merged; the available material and information are, however, insufficient, and intermediate specimens occur, so that they are for the present kept separate.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule pale yellow; pilosity yellow, sparse. Postclypeus weakly to moderately inflated, Pcl/W 0.24–0.28. Mandibular apical tooth rather short or slightly long, La/Li 0.64–0.73, Ra/Ri 0.86–0.93; in surface view the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible is separated by a distinct notch from the molar ridge, the composite ratio La/Li·Lm 10.28–13.06; the first marginal tooth of the right mandible is inserted slightly behind the line from the apical tooth to the second marginal tooth, the anterior margins of the first and second marginal teeth about equal or the former slightly shorter, Ra/Ri·Rm 13.68–17.10. Fore tibia slender, Ti/Tw 5.35–5.90; third apical spur very small, reduced, even absent in some specimens, but rarely absent in all specimens of the same nest series. The midgut–hindgut junction is slightly longer than diagonal; the enteric valve seat has a very short neck and is nearly dorsal in the unopened abdomen; the first enteric valve cushion is sclerotized along its whole length, about half of it projecting beyond the tips of the spines of the other positions, the swollen end ringed by 23–38 slender spines (mean 29.4), small spines scattered on the stalk and on the concave surface of the swollen end, the base of the stalk with transverse wrinkles; the cushions of the other positions bear 1–10 slender curved spines (mean 5.1), weakly hooked at the tip, with smaller spines scattered over the rest of their length; no perceptible spines occur on the membranous wall of the valve between or outside the cushions.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule dark brown, darker above the ocelli and around the compound eyes; fontanelle elliptical or circular, smaller than the ocellus, its margin ill defined, sometimes nearly triangular, flat or slightly concave, brown or pale to almost yellowish white; central spot circular, flat, smaller than the fontanelle, slightly paler than the head capsule; postclypeus dark brown, labrum brown; frontal mark distinct, flat, semicircular, concolorous with the head capsule; antennae pale brown. Pronotum and meso- and metanotum dark brown, the dark transverse sutures weakly developed, especially on the mesonotum; femora and tibiae pale brown, tarsi yellow. Abdominal tergites and sternites brown, the median part of the sternites paler, dorsolateral and ventrolateral spiracles darker, dark brown; cerci pale yellowish brown. Posterior margin of head capsule unevenly rounded, distinctly undulate; ocelli rather small, their distance from the compound eye slightly less to slightly more than their own minimum diameter; postclypeus moderately to strongly inflated, Pcl/W 0.28–0.34, posterior margin evenly rounded, median suture weakly developed or almost absent. Mandibular apical tooth short, La/Li 0.50–0.60, Ra/Ri 0.70–0.84; in surface view the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible lies far from the molar ridge, the composite ratio La/Li·Lm 5.33; the apical and marginal teeth of the right mandible are inserted nearly in line, the anterior margins of the first and second marginal teeth about equal in length. Meso- and metanotum of moderate width at the constriction, M/W 0.28–0.34. Cephalic pilosity brown, felt-like, with uneven outstanding setae.
